newsitem.title: USA: Azerbaijan set to move oil through Russia pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Azerbaijan set to move oil through Russia pipeline.

text.p: Azerbaijan state oil oil company Socar expects to begin moving oil to the Black Sea through Russian pipeline company Transneft's pipeline system in the first quarter, an Azerbaijan oil executive said Wednesday.

Ilham Aliyev, first vice president of Azerbaijani state-owned oil company Socar, said the company plans to move 150,000 tons per quarter, or about 500,000 to 600,000 tons a year, through the line while awaiting production from an international consortium to produce oil in the country's Caspian Sea fields.
"Azerbaijan oil will be on the world market earlier than expected," Aliyev told reporters following a speech at Cambridge Energy Research Associates energy forum.
Transneft had recently said only oil produced by the consortium could move through the Russian pipeline, but earlier this week said the Azerbailani oil could move as early as May.

Aliyev said the delay was caused in part by concerns for assuring the safety of Transneft workers along a section of the pipeline in Chechnya. Under the transport agreement, 5 million tonnes of crude should be flowing through the pipeline by 2002, he said.
Socar President Natig Aliyev is set to meet with Transeft officials in Moscow in early March to iron out the transport arrangement, Ilham Aliyev said.
